newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Solidarity leads before parliamentary polls.
newsitem.headline: Polish Solidarity leads before parliamentary polls.

text.p: Poland's opposition Solidarity alliance (AWS) took the lead from the ruling ex-communists just a month before general elections, an opinion poll released on Monday showed.

The survey showed the AWS was backed by 28 percent of voters, three points more than in the institute's previous poll on July 19-20. The ex-communists' (SLD) ranking slipped by one point to 25 percent.
The poll was commissioned by the Rzeczpospolita daily and carried out between August 9-10 by the private PBS agency.
PBS said July's catastrophic floods had not significantly harmed the popularity of the SLD, although it could have hampered its ability to attract new voters.

"The small changes in support for the SLD are within statistical error. The SLD electorate is very stable, but there is a trend of the AWS increasing its voter base," deputy head of PBS Ryszard Pienkowski, told Reuters.

Earlier opinion polls indicated many Poles were dissatisfied by the way the government had handled the flood crisis, in which 54 people died, but Pienkowski said this apparently did not apply to the SLD's electorate.
